title: dev.qory.run.exited
description: The run ended: Forager's close of the run wrote the outcome its caller gave, or the run ended without a close, the gateway ending it or a resend of its record finding it lost. The result of the run and its last event. Every run.exited contains state, how the run ended: succeeded, failed or cancelled, and Forager writes exit_code too, the run's exit code: the exit status of the run's last session, 124 when the run's time limit was reached, -1 when no session ran, -1 with gateway_lost and in every dev.qory.run.exited the gateway writes for a run on its link. The schema fixes state to failed and exit_code to -1 with gateway_lost and with no_session, and does not require exit_code, so records written before, of runs with no process, still validate. The gateway's dev.qory.run.exited of a run it ends has exit_code -1, and the state of its ending, the README's §The events, How a run ends; the session's record of the code of the gateway's 410 has the exit code of the run's last session, -1 when a session was open at the 410; a starter's reason comes with any state, so the schema fixes neither for those reasons. How each session ended is its dev.qory.session.exited: when the gateway ends the run while a join is open, or the resend of a record writes gateway_lost for a run with an open session, that session's dev.qory.session.exited comes first, with the same state, reason and exit_code -1.

state.description: How the run ended, on every run.exited. succeeded: the run ended well; failed: it ended badly; cancelled: it was stopped before it said how it went. The close writes the state its caller gives, any of the three; how a session's runtime exit decides a state is dev.qory.session.exited's rule. A run its starter ended with an outcome has that outcome. Forager's endings: cancelled with timeout, interrupted and stopped; failed with no_session, image_missing, session_lost, gateway_lost and batch_refused.

exit_code.description: The run's exit code: the exit status of the run's last session, the exit_code of its dev.qory.session.exited; 124 when the run's time limit was reached; -1 when no session ran; and -1 when the gateway ends the run, which holds no exit status of a session's, and in the session's record of the gateway's 410 when a session was open at the 410. Forager writes it on every run.exited; records written before may lack it.

signal.description: The signal that killed the runtime, when one did: SIGKILL, SIGTERM.

reason.description: Why the run ended, when the close's outcome has a reason, when the run ended without a close, or the reason its starter gave: an open code, a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and _, up to 64 characters. Forager's codes are reserved: timeout, interrupted, no_session, stopped, session_lost, gateway_lost, batch_refused and run_closed; and so are the old names quiet, credential_expired, credential_check_unreachable, credential_check_invalid, run_ended_at_issuer, issuer_unreachable and issuer_answer_invalid, which Forager never writes, kept so that records written before still validate. Any other code is the starter's, carried as given; a starter's reason that equals a reserved code, or that is not a code, is dropped, its outcome kept: the run has no reason, but for a cancelled run, whose reason is then stopped, as when its starter gave none. timeout: the run's time limit was reached, during its host work or a session, whose runtime the session stopped; exit_code is 124. interrupted: the run was stopped from where it was started, a Ctrl-C or a signal to the program that opened the run, before its close; exit_code is the last session's, -1 when no session ran. no_session: the run was closed with no join, after its host work failed, such as a fetch or a compose; state is failed and exit_code -1. stopped: the run's starter ended the run and gave no outcome. session_lost: the gateway heard nothing from the session for 3 × its heartbeat interval. gateway_lost: the gateway was lost before the run's end was recorded, because Forager died, and the event is written after the run has ended, by whatever sends the record again; duration_ms runs to the last event recorded. batch_refused: the gateway refused a batch from the run's session (§The gateway's link); the gateway writes it in its record, and the session in the session's record. The close writes timeout, interrupted and no_session, and posts them; only in the session's record it records the reason of the gateway's 410, and run_closed, the gateway's 410 to a run already ended there, after the session's final event or when the gateway stops, which no other record holds. The resend of a record writes gateway_lost, and the gateway the others. A session's batch on the link contains no reason of Forager's but timeout, interrupted and no_session, and no reason of the starter's; it may contain image_missing, the refusal code, which the close writes when its caller gives it after the fetch of an image its registry, or the registry's mirror, does not have, failed with exit_code -1 in a run with no join. Absent when the close's outcome has none, such as a run whose last session's runtime exited by itself, and when the starter gave an outcome other than cancelled with no reason or with a reserved one.

quiet_seconds.description: A quiet period in seconds, which Forager no longer writes: present only with the old reason quiet, in records written before, and absent otherwise.

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds from run.started to the run's end.
